precepts.text: The wave offering was waved in the hands of Aaron and his sons before the Lord and then burnt on the altar, and the wave breast and heave shoulder were the priests' part from the children of Israel for ever.
precepts.point: It is a covenant of salt for ever before the Lord, unto Aaron and to his seed with him, the children that come after them.

note.label: Numbers 18: The Charge and Portion of the Priests and Levites

precepts.why:
The flesh of the firstlings was the priest's, “as the wave breast and as the right shoulder are thine”, and all the heave offerings of the holy things were given to Aaron and his sons and daughters by a statute for ever, to the lineage of the Levites. Exodus 29 shows how the wave offering and the heave offering were done.

“And thou shalt put all in the hands of Aaron, and in the hands of his sons; and shalt wave them for a wave offering before the Lord. And thou shalt receive them of their hands, and burn them upon the altar for a burnt offering, for a sweet savour before the Lord.” The wave offering was put in the hands of Aaron and his sons and waved, meaning shaken, before the Lord; then it was received of their hands and burnt upon the altar. Each had a different way it was waved or lifted up to the Most High before it was actually burnt and offered to the Lord.

“And thou shalt take the breast of the ram of Aaron’s consecration, and wave it for a wave offering before the Lord: and it shall be thy part.” The breast of the ram of consecration was waved and became the priest's part. The breast of the wave offering and “the shoulder of the heave offering, which is waved, and which is heaved up”, were sanctified, “And it shall be Aaron’s and his sons’ by a statute for ever from the children of Israel.”

That is the wave breast and the right shoulder of Numbers 18, the priests' part from the children of Israel for ever, “a covenant of salt for ever before the Lord unto thee and to thy seed with thee”, the children that come after them.

precepts.text: All the heave offerings of the holy things are given to the priest and his sons by a statute for ever; it is a covenant of salt before the Lord.
precepts.point: Moses gave the tribute, the Lord's heave offering, unto Eleazar the priest, as the Lord commanded Moses. The heave offerings belong to the priesthood by statute forever, a covenant of salt, because Aaron and Levi have no inheritance in the land; the Most High is their part and their inheritance.

note.label: Numbers 31: Vengeance on the Midianites

precepts.why:
Moses gave the tribute, “which was the Lord’s heave offering, unto Eleazar the priest.” It went to the priest by law: “All the heave offerings of the holy things, which the children of Israel offer unto the Lord, have I given thee, and thy sons and thy daughters with thee, by a statute for ever: it is a covenant of salt for ever before the Lord unto thee and to thy seed with thee.”

The heave offerings belong to the priesthood by a statute for ever, a covenant of salt. The Lord’s heave offering out of the spoil of Midian was Eleazar’s by that covenant.

precepts.text: Aaron has no inheritance in their land; the Lord is his part and his inheritance among the children of Israel.
precepts.point: Moses gave the tribute, the Lord's heave offering, unto Eleazar the priest, as the Lord commanded Moses. The heave offerings belong to the priesthood by statute forever, a covenant of salt, because Aaron and Levi have no inheritance in the land; the Most High is their part and their inheritance.

note.label: Numbers 31: Vengeance on the Midianites

precepts.why:
Why do the heave offerings go to the priest? “And the Lord spake unto Aaron, Thou shalt have no inheritance in their land, neither shalt thou have any part among them: I am thy part and thine inheritance among the children of Israel.”

Aaron has no inheritance in the land; the Most High is his part and his inheritance. So the Lord’s heave offering of the spoil, given to Eleazar the priest, is the priesthood’s portion in place of land.

precepts.text: The children of Levi are given all the tenth in Israel for an inheritance, for the service of the tabernacle of the congregation.
precepts.point: Moses gave the tribute, the Lord's heave offering, unto Eleazar the priest, as the Lord commanded Moses. The heave offerings belong to the priesthood by statute forever, a covenant of salt, because Aaron and Levi have no inheritance in the land; the Most High is their part and their inheritance.

note.label: Numbers 31: Vengeance on the Midianites

precepts.why:
“And, behold, I have given the children of Levi all the tenth in Israel for an inheritance, for their service which they serve, even the service of the tabernacle of the congregation.”

Levi has no inheritance in the land either; the tenth in Israel is their inheritance, for the service of the tabernacle. The heave offering to Eleazar and the tenth to Levi are the same order: the Most High is their part, and the offerings of Israel sustain those who serve him.

precepts.text: The Levites are taken from among the children of Israel as a gift to do the service of the tabernacle; that is why every tribe gave them cities.
precepts.point: The commandment was fulfilled when Israel came into the land: the heads of the fathers of the Levites came to Eleazar the priest and Joshua at Shiloh and claimed the cities the Lord commanded by the hand of Moses.

note.label: Numbers 35: The Cities of the Levites and the Cities of Refuge

precepts.why:
The tribes were commanded to give the Levites cities to dwell in out of their own inheritance, with suburbs round about them. Why did the Levites need cities inside every tribe’s territory? “And I, behold, I have taken your brethren the Levites from among the children of Israel: to you they are given as a gift for the Lord, to do the service of the tabernacle of the congregation.”

The Levites were taken from among the children of Israel as a gift, to do the service of the tabernacle. Every tribe needed that service done among them, so the Levites had to be spread out through all the children of Israel. That is why every tribe gave them cities.

precepts.text: Thou shalt have no inheritance in their land; I am thy part and thine inheritance among the children of Israel.
precepts.point: Only unto the tribe of Levi he gave none inheritance; the sacrifices of the Lord God of Israel made by fire are their inheritance. The Most High had already said the same thing way back to Aaron, that Levi would have no inheritance in the land but would live among the people, and what was stated back then is being carried out in what we are reading now.

note.label: Joshua 13: Much Land Yet to Be Possessed

precepts.why:
“Only unto the tribe of Levi he gave none inheritance; the sacrifices of the Lord God of Israel made by fire are their inheritance, as he said unto them.” Where did he say it? Way back to Aaron: “Thou shalt have no inheritance in their land, neither shalt thou have any part among them: I am thy part and thine inheritance among the children of Israel.”

Levi would have no inheritance in the land; he would live among the people, and the Lord himself would be his part. What was stated back then to Aaron is being carried out in what we are reading now: while the Reubenites, the Gadites and the half tribe of Manasseh hold the inheritance Moses gave them beyond Jordan eastward, Levi's inheritance is the sacrifices of the Lord made by fire, exactly as he said.

precepts.text: The Levites do the service of the tabernacle, and among the children of Israel they have no inheritance.
precepts.point: The Levites have no part among you, for the priesthood of the Lord is their inheritance. The Levites were well taken care of; they dwelt in the suburbs of the cities and had the best of everything.

note.label: Joshua 18: The Lots Cast at Shiloh

precepts.why:
“But the Levites have no part among you; for the priesthood of the Lord is their inheritance”. That was set long before: “But the Levites shall do the service of the tabernacle of the congregation, and they shall bear their iniquity: it shall be a statute for ever throughout your generations, that among the children of Israel they have no inheritance.”

The Levites do the service of the tabernacle, and that is their portion. It is a statute for ever, so no lot was cast for Levi among the seven parts. And the Levites were well taken care of; they dwelt in the suburbs of the cities and had the best of everything.

precepts.text: The priesthood was given to Aaron and his sons as a gift; the stranger that came near was to be put to death, so the office was never the king's to seize.
precepts.point: The lesson to all of us is to stay in the spirit, stay humble, and never forget who put you in the position you are in. When a man becomes lifted up he loses his humility and forgets who set him where he is. Uzziah was a leper to the day of his death and dwelt in a separate house, cut off from the house of the Most High.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 26: Uzziah Prospers, Then Pride Brings Him Low

precepts.why:
The Most High said to Aaron, “thou and thy sons with thee shall keep your priest’s office for every thing of the altar, and within the vail”, and “I have given your priest’s office unto you as a service of gift: and the stranger that cometh nigh shall be put to death.” The priesthood was given to Aaron and his sons as a gift, and the office was never the king’s to seize.

That is what Azariah and the fourscore priests told Uzziah: “It appertaineth not unto thee, Uzziah, to burn incense unto the Lord, but to the priests the sons of Aaron, that are consecrated to burn incense: go out of the sanctuary; for thou hast trespassed”. He came nigh where he did not belong, and “the Lord had smitten him.”

points: The Lord told Aaron that he and his sons and his father's house would bear the iniquity of the sanctuary and of their priesthood; that was their job. This explains who should minister in the tabernacle after Israel's cry in the last chapter.

note.label: Numbers 18: The Charge and Portion of the Priests and Levites

points: The tribe of Levi was joined unto Aaron to minister unto him and keep the charge of the tabernacle, their jobs; only they were not to come nigh the vessels of the sanctuary and the altar, the ark of the covenant and the different vessels, that neither they nor the priests die.

note.label: Numbers 18: The Charge and Portion of the Priests and Levites

points: The Levites were given to Aaron as a gift for the Lord, to do the service of the tabernacle; Aaron and his sons kept the priest's office for every thing of the altar and within the vail. The stranger that cometh nigh shall be put to death: an Israelite not of Levi could not come near the tabernacle.

note.label: Numbers 18: The Charge and Portion of the Priests and Levites

points: The Lord gave Aaron the charge of the heave offerings of all the hallowed things of the children of Israel, by reason of the anointing, to him and his sons by an ordinance for ever.

note.label: Numbers 18: The Charge and Portion of the Priests and Levites

points: Of the most holy things reserved from the fire, every oblation, meat offering, sin offering, and trespass offering was most holy for Aaron and his sons; the priests kept a portion of it and ate it in the most holy place.

note.label: Numbers 18: The Charge and Portion of the Priests and Levites

points: The heave offering of their gift, with all the wave offerings of the children of Israel, was given to Aaron and his sons and his daughters by a statute for ever; every one that is clean in the house could eat of it. This is what the children of Israel gave for the Levites.

note.label: Numbers 18: The Charge and Portion of the Priests and Levites

points: All the best of the oil, the best of the wine, and the wheat, the firstfruits which they offered unto the Lord, were given to the priests; whatsoever is first ripe in the land was theirs, and every one that was clean in the house could eat of it.

note.label: Numbers 18: The Charge and Portion of the Priests and Levites

points: Every thing devoted in Israel was theirs.

note.label: Numbers 18: The Charge and Portion of the Priests and Levites

points: Every thing that openeth the matrix in all flesh, whether of men or beasts, was the Lord's; the firstborn was to be offered. Nevertheless the firstborn of man was surely redeemed, because you would not sacrifice the firstborn of our people, and the firstling of unclean beasts was redeemed also.

note.label: Numbers 18: The Charge and Portion of the Priests and Levites

points: Verse 16 explains how you redeem them: those to be redeemed from a month old were redeemed for the money of five shekels, after the shekel of the sanctuary, which is twenty gerahs; twenty gerahs equal one shekel.

note.label: Numbers 18: The Charge and Portion of the Priests and Levites

points: But the firstling of a cow, a sheep, or a goat was not redeemed, because those you could sacrifice: they are holy; their blood was sprinkled upon the altar and their fat burnt for an offering made by fire, for a sweet savour unto the Lord.

note.label: Numbers 18: The Charge and Portion of the Priests and Levites

points: The flesh of them was the priest's, as the wave breast and as the right shoulder; all the heave offerings of the holy things which the children of Israel offered unto the Lord were given to Aaron and his sons and his daughters by a statute for ever, to the lineage of the Levites.

Exodus 29 shows how the wave offering and the heave offering were done. The wave offering was put in the hands of Aaron and his sons and waved, meaning shaken, before the Lord; then it was received of their hands and burnt upon the altar. Each had a different way it was waved or lifted up to the Most High before it was actually burnt and offered to the Lord, and the breast of the ram of consecration was waved and became the priest's part.
It is a covenant of salt for ever before the Lord, unto Aaron and to his seed with him, the children that come after them.

note.label: Numbers 18: The Charge and Portion of the Priests and Levites

points: The Lord told Aaron: thou shalt have no inheritance in their land, neither any part among them; I am thy part and thine inheritance among the children of Israel. The Levites had no inheritance of land to pass down; the Most High said, I will be taking care of you.

note.label: Numbers 18: The Charge and Portion of the Priests and Levites

points: The Lord gave the children of Levi all the tenth in Israel for an inheritance. This is the tithe: the tenth part was given to the Levites for their service which they served, the service of the tabernacle of the congregation, their sacrificing and teaching of the laws.
That tenth went to the children of Levi, and it was done away with when Christ came and died and took that priesthood; we no longer give that tenth to Levi.

note.label: Numbers 18: The Charge and Portion of the Priests and Levites

points: The children of Israel were not to come nigh the tabernacle of the congregation, lest they bear sin and die; it was a sin for the other tribes of Israel to come near the tabernacle, on pain of death. All the work to be done in the tabernacle was committed unto the Levites, and they bore their iniquity, a statute for ever.

note.label: Numbers 18: The Charge and Portion of the Priests and Levites

points: When the Levites took of the children of Israel the tithes given them for their inheritance, they offered up of it an heave offering for the Lord, even a tenth part of the tithe: after the Levites got their tenth, the Most High wanted his tenth part of that, which they had to offer up.

note.label: Numbers 18: The Charge and Portion of the Priests and Levites

points: Their heave offering was reckoned unto them as though it were the corn of the threshingfloor and the fulness of the winepress, and the Lord's heave offering out of all their tithes was given to Aaron the priest; out of all their gifts they offered every heave offering of the Lord, of all the best thereof, even the hallowed part.

note.label: Numbers 18: The Charge and Portion of the Priests and Levites

points: When they had heaved the best thereof from it, they could eat it in every place, they and their households, for it was their reward for their service in the tabernacle of the congregation; and they bore no sin by reason of it when they heaved the best of it, neither polluted the holy things of the children of Israel, lest they die.
